column1: # The ZAP rule file of the security round (web.ui_baseline and web.api_baseline,
# deploy/security/README.md, "The rule files"). ZAP's own format: one rule per line, three
# fields separated by a tab: the rule (plugin) id, the action, the rule's name in
# parentheses. A line that starts with '#' is a comment.
# Actions: FAIL fails the row (an alert of this rule should never be raised on Tenko); WARN
# reports the alert as a finding of the release report for the triage; IGNORE drops the
# alert. A rule that is not listed is WARN (ZAP's default). Every IGNORE carries its reason
# in the comment lines above it. Both rows report and do not block a release until this
# file has been through two releases without a new finding of High or above (section 4.4 of
# docs/plans/security-audit-plan.md).
# Change a rule with its reason in the same commit, as narrowly as ZAP allows (a rule id,
# never a category). The ZAP version's full rule list is in every bundle
# (scan/zap-ui/rules-default.tsv), for checking this file against a new version.
# FAIL: the response headers every answer carries (crates/tenko-api/src/middleware/headers.rs:
# CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, the
# three cross-origin policies, HSTS over HTTPS) and the session cookie's flags (HttpOnly,
# Secure, SameSite=Strict).
# FAIL 10063 and 90004 since the fix of SF-0008 and SF-0009 (the report of 0.0.10): every
# answer carries Permissions-Policy (the features the interface never uses denied, the
# clipboard and the passkey ceremonies allowed to its own origin only) and
# Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy,
# so a missing one anywhere is a regression of the middleware, not a finding to triage.
# FAIL: what a single-origin application with no third-party script and no server banner
# never shows.

column1: # WARN: findings the triage reads and decides.
# IGNORE 10116: the alert says the ZAP release is older than the newest. The image is
# pinned by digest on purpose (compose.yml), so a scan never changes under the round; a
# new ZAP version arrives as a commit that moves the tag and the digest together.
# IGNORE 10109: the alert says the site is a single-page application and suggests the
# AJAX spider. The web interface is one by design; the passive rules still see every
# response the spider fetches, and web.api_baseline covers the API the application calls.
# IGNORE 100000: the alert says a client error (4xx) was returned. The API scan imports the
# OpenAPI document and sends placeholder identifiers and bodies, so a 4xx answer is the API's
# correct refusal of them, one alert per path template and no weakness. The refusals that
# matter are checked elsewhere: web.unauth sends every operation without credentials and
# blocks on any answer but 401 or 403, and the FAIL rules above catch a missing header on
# those answers. 100001 (Unexpected Content-Type, Low) stays a WARN.
